newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila posts 4.8 bln peso public sector surplus.
newsitem.headline: Manila posts 4.8 bln peso public sector surplus.

text.p: The Philippines posted a 4.8 billion peso public sector surplus by the end of 1996, the final report submitted by the finance department said on Monday.
The final figure was 2.7 billion pesos higher than the preliminary level announced in February. The report did not give any reason for the big difference between the preliminary and final figures.
In a report to President Fidel Ramos, acting finance secretary Milwida Guevara said it was the first time the country was able to post a surplus since it started monitoring the sector in 1985.
The government was earlier projecting a balanced public sector position for 1996.
The public sector includes the national and local government units, government pension funds, government financial institutions, government owned and controlled corporations and the Central Bank.
Guevara said the lower deficit incurred by state corporations and higher cash positions of government financial institutions helped boost the surplus.
"The surplus generated by the consolidated public sector helped dampen inflation and interest rates," she added.
